non_blocking_findings.title: The shipped suite does not kill 'drop the refresh' (JM1); goal (b) rests on the AC7 mutation, not on a shipped check
non_blocking_findings.detail: Removing `ident.occlusion.refresh(demo.camera)` from eye_clear leaves the shipped suite green (.godot/tmp/7an.oBWzTEMU/jm1.log: 23 passed, 0 failures), because update_candidates() refreshes the BVH immediately before the check in the shipped order. The refresh is load-bearing only under a reordering: JM1 + the AC7 permutation (.godot/tmp/7an.EycsmDm8/jm1ac7.log: 52 passed, 3 failures) fails 'the fixed eye looks ahead past the ship' at the first stop while the second stop's passes vacuously - the two stops disagree. So the AC7 acceptance criterion (the executor's own mutation) is the only guard on the property; CI would not notice a later removal of the refresh.
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Accept as is. If the row's owner wants CI-grade protection for goal (b), the cheap form is a second assertion that asks the BVH before and after a refresh and requires them to agree, inside tests/test_free_nav_stop.gd. Not a blocker: the shipped code carries the refresh and AC7 measures it.

non_blocking_findings.title: Two clauses of the new free-nav checks have no shipped coverage (JM2, JM3)
non_blocking_findings.detail: 'and demo.sky.starfield.pinned_ids.is_empty()' (JM2) and 'lit[0] >= 1' (JM3) are each removable with the suite staying green, because in this flow no pin ever happens and the helper always finds the destination's rows. The controls show both clauses are live: JM2c (a pin injected, clause intact) fails 'its catalogue row is dark ... (1 rows, lit [], 1 pins)' and JM3c (the helper finds no row) fails '... (0 rows, lit [], 0 pins)'. JM3b - the double mutant, re-run by this judge because the previous session's wall clock cut it off - stays green ('free-nav-stop: 23 passed, 0 failures', 114 s of 900 s), which is the point: with '>= 0' the check would go blind to a helper that stops finding the rows.

non_blocking_findings.title: The SSI pin check's three clauses are individually redundant; a count-only check would be blind to the no-pin case

Each alone still catches the no-pin mutant (JM-A3b and JM-A4b both fail with 'a pinned destination is offered once, as its pin row (1 candidates)'), but with both dropped the vmag-99 mutant survives (JM-A6b: 60 passed, 0 failures). non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Accept as is. The redundancy is a property of a three-clause check, and the shipped form is the strongest of the three variants measured.

non_blocking_findings.title: sky_hides duplicates product logic; the drift mitigation is verified (JM-A8), not merely asserted

non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Accept. The comment naming the mirrored function is the right mitigation and it now has mutation evidence behind it.

judgement.do_the_new_checks_fail_for_the_right_rea: Yes, and each fails with its own message. The two sky checks fail together with the I check under AC6 and with the right candidate counts (43); the dark-row check fails under AC8 while the I check still passes with 44 candidates - the layer the I check cannot see is exactly the layer it catches; the pin check fails under AC9 with '(0 candidates)', the duplicate-count reason, not an incidental error; the eye check fails twice under AC7 and under AC10 with the blocked-sightline reason. judgement.surviving_mutants: Four of the seventeen judge-side mutants survive, all in the same family: they weaken or remove an assertion inside a shipped check rather than break a product behaviour. JM1 (drop the refresh), JM2 (drop the pins clause), JM3 (weaken 'at least one row'), JM3b (their double), JM-A3/A4/A6 (weaken the SSI pin check) and JM-A6b. Each of the four new/changed checks is killed by a product mutant (AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9s, AC10) and by a judge-side control (JM-A1, JM-A2, JM2c, JM3c, JM-A3b, JM-A4b, JM1+AC7). So the checks are real guards; what the survivors show is that the shipped suite does not defend the checks' own defensive clauses. That is a hardening note (NB1-NB3), not a blocker: the row's three goals are met and each is backed by a measured killer.
